title: A knockdown lasts 0.7 to 1.5 s instead of 1.0 to 2.5 s
pillar: P4 a hit is a choice with a price, for both men (R-0049: a tackle is an event, not a rhythm)
hypothesis: A knocked-down skater lies 60 to 150 frames by the size of the hit (game.contact.down_frames_min / max, JamCartridge.h:400-401; UJamSim::ResolveContact lerps between them). The planning hand lies 7.3 s of a 120 s match at pro (3.7 knockdowns at 2.0 s each); the play it was in lasts 2.4 s, so a knockdown outlasts it: the hit costs the puck, the place AND a wait. With 40 to 90 frames the knockdown still costs the puck and the place (the two-second release grace after getting up is kept), and the wait is two thirds of a second to a second and a half. The number is everybody's (bots lie shorter too), so the human's own hits buy less time. Expected: seconds on the ice down by about 40 % for every hand (T6: at most 5 s a match at pro); knockdowns a match about the same; wins about the same (it cuts both ways); the body check and the cross-check worth a little less to the hand that throws them.
tempo: seconds down against the length of a possession: 1.0-2.5 s : 2.4 s becomes 0.67-1.5 s : 2.4 s

why: The target moved as predicted and nothing else moved beyond the noise. Seconds on the ice a match, planning hand at pro: novice 10.7 to 6.1, regular 7.3 to 5.3, good 6.0 to 3.5; at all-star regular 8.0 to 5.1; thirdjam's regular hand at pro 11.6 to 8.2 (T6 asks at most 5 s at pro: the regular planning hand is at 5.3). Knockdowns a match did not fall (3.7 to 4.3 for the regular planning hand: a man who is up sooner can be hit again sooner), so T6's other half (at most 3) is not met and is the levels' work (who throws how many hits: round 3). Wins: planning hand at pro -3.3 +-6.3 / +5.0 +-8.7 / +1.7 +-2.9 (regular / novice / good), all-star +8.3 +-7.6; thirdjam's regular +6.7 +-8.9, good +8.3 +-8.0. One cell at two standard errors: thirdjam's novice at pro 20 to 8.3 % (-11.7 +-5.9); one of fourteen cells, the scripted hand, noted and not a reason to reject (the Director's ruling on the second opinion).
owner_line: When you are knocked down you are back on your skates in about a second, not two. You still lose the puck and your place; you no longer watch the play leave.
